# Vanishr

> Vanishr is an independent, open-source Android development app for end-to-end encrypted disappearing text, photos and invite-only groups. It is not independently security-audited and is not recommended for real sensitive conversations yet.

## Official public pages

- [Vanishr](https://vanishr-download.vercel.app/): Product overview and current development status.
- [Android download](https://vanishr-download.vercel.app/android/): Signed APK, requirements, installation, checksums, current release and matching source.
- [Security model](https://vanishr-download.vercel.app/security/): Encryption, independent contact verification, expiry, metadata and limitations.
- [App and website privacy policy](https://vanishr-download.vercel.app/privacy/): Accounts, encrypted content and metadata, Google sign-in/FCM, automatic Remote Photos, retention, deletion and separate opt-in website analytics.
- [Delete account](https://vanishr-download.vercel.app/delete-account/): Email deletion requests without reinstalling, ownership verification, in-app deletion, data removed and retention exceptions.
- [Terms and community standards](https://vanishr-download.vercel.app/terms/): Acceptable use, blocking/reporting, child sexual abuse and exploitation prevention, and the public escalation contact.
- [Child-safety standards](https://vanishr-download.vercel.app/terms/#child-safety): Prohibited CSAE/CSAM, metadata-only reporting and human escalation responsibilities.

## Important distinctions

- Android 9 or later with a phone screen lock is required. There is no iOS or browser chat client.
- Direct messages use official libsignal sessions; private groups use libsignal sender keys with explicit verified-owner trust. Vanishr is not affiliated with or endorsed by Signal or Google.
- Usernames discover contacts but do not prove identity. Ordinary contacts require independent safety-number verification. Only the official signed-app pin introduces the sole human admin, Vanishr / @vanishr, without a manual identity prompt; this does not grant photo permissions.
- Profile photos are exchanged only by mutually added, verified direct contacts. They never appear in username search. Group membership alone grants no photo access.
- View-once and timed expiry cannot stop a malicious recipient from preserving a copy. Do not describe disappearing messages as impossible to save.
- The relay sees account/routing metadata and ciphertext, not client plaintext or private decryption keys.
- Accounts use a username, optional display name, random account UUID and password verifier or Google subject. Vanishr does not store Google email, name or photo. The admin sees new-registration metadata, not unrelated conversations.
- Remote Photos is admin-requested and requires independently verified direct contacts, Android permissions and an unlocked owner phone at startup. Eligible requests are automatically accepted; there is no active per-request Allow prompt or owner Auto-allow toggle. An ongoing foreground-service notification offers End access. Sessions last at most 15 minutes and may continue after the owner locks the phone or backgrounds the app. Google Play consent/permission review remains unresolved; do not call this Play-ready.
- Version 0.4.6 (code 27) is the account-safety candidate; 0.4.5 does not have its in-app deletion, Block user and Report user/content controls. Use the deletion page's email route if controls are unavailable. A matching updated relay is required.
- Account deletion removes durable account/device/public-key/membership data and safety reports submitted by or targeting the account; no post-deletion safety-report retention exception applies. Deleting the pinned admin clears the entire undeliverable report queue. A separate minimal database receipt retains only the deletion proof's SHA-256 digest, original random account UUID, PENDING/DELETED state and creation/expiry times for a fixed 24-hour window from creation, surviving account deletion and temporary-store resets. Checks/retries do not extend it; access expires at the deadline and expired rows are purged every minute while the service runs. Other people's delivered copies follow original expiry; queued ciphertext remains bounded by existing lifetimes no longer than 24 hours. The immutable random admin UUID reservation may survive to prevent reassignment.
- Initial deletion requires fresh account-only password or Google authentication. The client must save a random deletion proof and original UUID in encrypted storage before that request. Failed cleanup can leave DELETING state with previous credentials revoked. The saved proof supports status/retry of an already-started deletion without a bearer token; it cannot start deleting an active/different account. Only explicit DELETED confirmation matching the original UUID permits local account cleanup; missing/expired proof and arbitrary 401/404 responses never prove completion. Google reauthentication of saved accounts must match the expected existing UUID, not create a new account. Never email a deletion proof.
- Accepted reports expire within 30 days and require human review, not guaranteed moderation. Without an enabled pinned admin account, new in-app reports fail with 503 safety_review_unavailable. Public privacy, deletion and child-safety contact: richardhenryjames64@gmail.com. Never send credentials or private/illegal content, or post personal information to public GitHub issues.
- The Android app has no analytics SDK. Optional website analytics is a separate consent choice and receives no chat data.
- The matching release source archive is authoritative for a signed APK; repository HEAD may lag. Functional tests are not an independent security audit.

This optional summary helps readers locate public facts. It is not a special indexing protocol or a guarantee of inclusion in AI answers.
